constraints: t1 != t2 and t1 != t3 and t1 != t4 and t2 != t3 and t2 != t4 and t3 != t4
solution: Write down the factors. The first coefficient ${=a}$ has the factor pairs $1\times{=a}$ and ${=p}\times{=r}$. The constant term ${=c}$ has only the factor pair $1\times{=c}$.

In ${=a}x^{2}-{=m}x+{=c}$ the constant term is positive and the middle term is negative. The two constants in the brackets multiply to give $+{=c}$, so they have the same sign, and a positive pair would give a positive middle term, so both constants are negative. Both brackets therefore contain minus signs.

Set out the possible pairs of brackets. Use each pair of first-term factors with the constants $1$ and ${=c}$ placed both ways round: $(x-1)({=a}x-{=c})$, $(x-{=c})({=a}x-1)$, $({=p}x-1)({=r}x-{=c})$ and $({=p}x-{=c})({=r}x-1)$.
The trinomial has middle term $-{=m}x$, and only the brackets $({=p}x-{=u})({=r}x-{=w})$ give this. So ${=a}x^{2}-{=m}x+{=c}=({=p}x-{=u})({=r}x-{=w})$.

Check by multiplying out. The first terms give ${=p}x\times{=r}x={=a}x^{2}$, the last terms give $(-{=u})\times(-{=w})={=c}$, and the middle term is $-({=p}\times{=w}+{=u}\times{=r})x=-({=p*w}+{=u*r})x=-{=m}x$. This is the original trinomial, so the factorisation is correct.
notes: Harder than the book's typical exercise because the first coefficient is composite: a = p*r with p < r distinct primes (6, 10, 14, 15, 21), so a has exactly two factor pairs (1 x a and p x r), and the constant c is a prime coprime to a (never p or r), so it has the single pair 1 x c. That gives exactly four candidate bracket pairs, all listed and expanded in the solution; their middle terms a+c, ac+1, pc+r and p+rc are pairwise different (checked over the whole parameter space) and the answer is always one of the last two, i.e. the (p, r) split, as in the book's 6a^2-17a+5 = (2a-5)(3a-1). The constant is positive and the middle term negative, so both brackets carry minus signs. gcd(a, c) = 1 makes the trinomial primitive, so the factorisation into primitive brackets is unique up to order. Modelled on book question ex1-11-29v (page 39). Marker is expression/factorised, either bracket order. Every equation in every rendered solution was checked by evaluation over the whole parameter space (20 instances).
